Steepens the origin slope so near-zero even-spectrum eigenvalues lift faster. Verified in FP64 the schedule cuts iters 17->10 for equal sign quality (math is correct).

DOES SCALING HELP? YES, partially. Fixed-NS + a 2nd tf32x3_delta finish alone already cuts 17->12 (the extra finish is the dominant single lever). CANS scaling buys 2 MORE iters (12->10): at equal iters CANS has far better eigr margin (CANS-12 eigr 0.004 / 62% margin vs fixed-12 eigr 0.010 / 3%). So the win is CANS (17->10) layered on the 2nd-finish trick.

THE WALL: 9 iters FAILS on eigr (not orth) across reseeds -- eigr 0.017-0.019 > gate 0.0107, reseed-unsafe regardless of a0/head-split/f3. Confirms the brief's FP32-near-sigma-precision hypothesis: below ~10 iters the count is EIGENVALUE-RESOLUTION-bound (the fuzzy near-zero eigenvalue sign, |lambda|<~1e-3 unresolvable in TF32), NOT dynamic-range-bound -- scaling can't fix it. Aggressive a0<=0.1 blows orth to 0.1-4.8 (TF32 error from the ~1.6-1.9 overshoot). Both finishes MUST be tf32x3_delta (plain-tf32 or 'mix' 2nd finish -> orth 0.006-0.009 > gate, 640 fallback).
